name: SBH Health System (St. Barnabas Hospital)
catchment_source: data/processed/sbh_catchment_zips.csv (SBH Health System 2025-2027 Community Service Plan, p.21, primary service area ranked by patients)

data_sources.hvi_source: NYC DOHMH Heat Vulnerability Index by ZCTA 2020 (NYC Open Data 4mhf-duep); 1 = lowest, 5 = highest
data_sources.ac_source: NYC DOHMH EHDP indicator 2185 (NYC Housing and Vacancy Survey), % households with AC by sub-borough area

cooling_places.source_label: NYC Emergency Management Cool Options finder + NYC Parks rec centers + NYC FacDB libraries + OpenStreetMap (see data/raw/place/README.md)

detour_factor.source: ASSUMPTION: typical urban grid circuity (network ÷ straight-line distance ≈ 1.2-1.4); replaced by routed time when cooling_match.csv exists

older_or_mobility.source: Western et al., Age and Ageing 2025 (PMC12682371): older adults about 0.77-0.9 m/s (spec §4.4a.3)

naive_transit.source: ASSUMPTION: naive bus estimate (10-min wait + 12 km/h door-to-door); replaced by GTFS routing when available

contact_travel_columns.why: Conservative default: walking or subway (we don't know whether the contact has a car; free-flow driving is optimistic)
Only when no walk/subway route exists (e.g. out-of-area contacts: driving only)

alert_rules.heatrisk_scale: NWS/CDC HeatRisk 0-4 (0 green, 1 yellow, 2 orange, 3 red, 4 magenta)

call_today_if_uncovered.definition: No trusted contact close enough (routed travel within the time budget) AND (lives alone OR not opted in to safety alerts): automation can't reach anyone in time, so a human calls.

alert_rules.notes: Alerts fire only on high-risk days (spec §4.4 safety rules, §10.4 alert fatigue). Orange (2) calls only very-high-readiness patients; red (3) and magenta (4) add high-readiness patients that automation can't cover (no close-enough contact and living alone / not opted in); other high-readiness patients are covered by the automatic safety alert, cooling-place text, check-ins and contact escalation. Red and magenta trigger the automatic safety alert for high/very-high readiness. Heat cards are non-urgent education (no DND breakthrough), so they are not gated on the forecast. Thresholds are a team design choice (ASSUMPTION), tunable per health system.

escalation.t_max_source: Spec §4.4a.1 starting values: classic heat stroke mortality more than halves if cooled below 38.9 °C within 1 h (PMC10227888; Bouchama et al., Crit Care 2007); exertional: cool within 30 min. 45/60/90 min leave time for cooling and EMS. 'low' = 120 min is an ASSUMPTION (low-readiness patients are not enrolled in active escalation by default).

patient_app_or_sms.source: ASSUMPTION pending extraction: p90 notification response time from Pielot et al. MobileHCI 2014 (10.1145/2628363.2628364), Pielot et al. 2018, Mehrotra et al. CHI 2016 (spec §4.4a.4: medians still to extract). Replaced by the person's own p90 learned from check-ins.

patient_voice_call.source: ASSUMPTION: voice call needs retries (two attempts ~10 min apart).

older_adult_extra.source: ASSUMPTION: 0 min until older-adult phone response data is extracted (spec §4.4a.8); knob kept so it can be raised without code changes.

contact.source: ASSUMPTION pending extraction (same notification literature as above); 15 min matches the routing agent's contact rule (data/raw/routing/contacts_summary.json).

contacts.final_step: Clinic call list: a human (nurse / care manager) decides on a wellness check. The system never requests 911 or a wellness check on its own.
contacts.buddy_program: NYC Be a Buddy (verify) / clinic volunteer buddy

help_programs.ac_assistance: NYS HEAP Cooling Assistance (free or discounted air conditioner)
